chunks: Those without faith among the people of the Book, and those who worship idols, do not wish that good should come to you from your Lord. But God chooses whom He likes for His grace; and the bounty of God is infinite.
ai.seo_question: Why do the disbelievers not wish for good to come to the believers from God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of *al-Hasr* (restriction) of divine favor, illustrating how the People of the Book and polytheists envied the spiritual elevation and specific blessings granted to the Prophet and his followers. It underscores God's absolute sovereignty (*al-Ikhtiyar*) in bestowing mercy, reinforcing the Shia belief that divine selection is based on wisdom and worthiness rather than mere lineage or majority status. This highlights the contrast between human envy and divine grace, a key theme in understanding the status of the Ahl al-Bayt.
